measurement_scope: GitHub-hosted Test job start-to-completion; excludes queue and separate inbox-security/AI Agent jobs. Phase times use timestamped Nx graph boundaries; baseline test phase includes prerequisite builds.
limitations: Two passing baselines, one cold, two passing warm samples; no statistical or guaranteed speedup claim.
Cache-enabled scheduling builds prerequisites as a separate union, then runs tests without dependencies. Baseline lets Nx schedule builds and tests together; this may lose overlap on other workloads.
Cache-enabled builds normalize SENTRY_RELEASE and disable optional SENTRY_BUILD_TELEMETRY. Baselines retain ordinary environment policy; timings compare implementations, not cache reuse alone.
Dependency download caches were available in all samples. Cache-off here means only this compiled-output snapshot is off.
Tests, Rust compilation inside test commands, and runtime DID-auth preflight remain uncached.
Warm test phases were slower than cold; cold vs warm wall time does not establish an isolated reuse speedup.
Same-branch exact hits do not prove future PR/merge-queue reuse; no trusted main producer was added.
Earlier E2E warm preparation improved but backend/setup/test variability prevented a whole-workflow advantage over host-only.
